claims.text: The initial cast alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance under high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
Pack cementation aluminization at approximately 950–1050 °C for a few hours will enrich the alloy surface in aluminum.
The aluminization treatment will produce a continuous alumina surface scale during high-temperature exposure.
The alumina scale formed on aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will be adherent.
The aluminum-enriched surface will oxidize preferentially to form Al2O3.
The resulting alumina scale will be stable and slow-growing at approximately 1000 °C in air.
The alumina scale will act as a barrier to oxygen ingress.
Restricting oxygen ingress will limit deleterious internal oxidation.
The short-duration surface treatment will not significantly alter the alloy's bulk composition or microstructure.
The bulk microstructure is responsible for the alloy's useful mechanical performance.
Aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit significantly lower oxygen uptake than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr after approximately 100 hours at 1000 °C in air.
Aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit less overall oxide-scale formation than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will retain the untreated alloy's room-temperature tensile ductility.
Aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will retain the untreated alloy's 1000 °C yield strength.
The intervention will remain effective under mechanical loading at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
